rounds.text: Eighty Jewellers is demonstrating powerful relative strength with a score of 92 against the Nifty 500, alongside a positive twelve-month price return of 11.3% [E6, E7]. The technical picture confirms underlying momentum, characterized by a price sitting above its 200-day moving average and a bullish golden cross where the 50-day moving average trades above the 200-day [E5, E17]. Furthermore, rules-based screening awards the stock a BUY score of 68 out of 100, heavily supported by outperformance of 22% versus the Nifty 500 over a three-month period [E13, E15]. Fundamental tailwinds are firmly at the company's back, operating within a Consumer Durables sector tailwind score of +0.80, which benefits from robust sector median sales growth of 13.0% and profit growth of 17.0% [E18, E21, E22]. Management is actively capturing this macro strength by expanding its market size and presence in Bilaspur with exclusive new collections, backed by robust global demand for ethically sourced natural diamonds [E25, E26, E28]. Conceded: [E1] (promoter holding decreased from 100% in Mar 2022 to 73.53% in Mar 2026).

Eighty Jewellers Ltd carries severe structural and price risks that undermine its current valuation support. Most notably, promoter holding has eroded significantly, dropping by 26.47 percentage points from 100.00% in March 2022 down to 73.53% by March 2026 [E1]. This steady dilution of insider stake should give any prudent investor pause. Furthermore, the stock exhibits extreme volatility at 63.9% [E9], accompanied by a dismal Sharpe ratio of just 0.24 [E10] and a harrowing worst historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -66.7% [E8]. These figures highlight an asset prone to violent corrections, rendering the current price action highly precarious. Adding to the shareholder friction, the company has consistently withheld payouts, having declared no dividend during the audit year [E30] and actively choosing to bypass dividends to preserve funds [E31]. Conceded: [E6].

While the bear points to promoter stake reduction, ownership remains a robust 73.53% [E1], leaving insiders heavily incentivized alongside public shareholders. The high historical volatility [E9] and deep past drawdown [E8] are standard characteristics of high-momentum equities, and the asset is currently displaying true market leadership with a stellar relative-strength rating of 92 against the Nifty 500 [E6]. The absence of dividends [E30], [E31] is a deliberate growth strategy rather than a warning sign, as management actively retains capital to fund new branches, franchisees, and exclusive new collections [E24], [E28] that drive market share expansion in regions like Bilaspur [E26], [E28]. Conceded: [E10].

Conceded: [E1]. While 73.53% ownership remains, the bull dismisses the substantial 26.47 percentage point drop from 100% since March 2022 [E1], which represents a major and ongoing dilution of insider skin in the game. Furthermore, calling high volatility of 63.9% [E9] and a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -66.7% [E8] merely standard traits of momentum glosses over the poor risk-adjusted reality captured by a Sharpe ratio of just 0.24 [E10]. The bull frames zero dividend payouts [E30], [E31] as a deliberate growth strategy, but this retention of capital occurs against a backdrop of modest sector median ROCE sitting at just 9.9% [E23], raising questions about the efficiency of those reinvested funds. Finally, while management highlights branch expansions and regional demand in Bilaspur [E24], [E26], [E28], they simultaneously acknowledge a complex macroeconomic landscape of inflation, interest rates, and geopolitical tensions [E32], alongside a volatile gold market that makes future trajectories challenging to predict [E27].

Conceded: [E30], [E31]. While the bear critiques the retention of capital against a sector median ROCE of 9.9% [E23], the broader operational reality shows the company actively reinvesting to capture robust global demand for ethically sourced and certified natural diamonds [E25] and expanding its market share in Bilaspur with exclusive new collections [E28]. Conceded: [E1]. The bear highlights the reduction in promoter holdings [E1], but management remains heavily invested with a controlling 73.53% stake [E1] while driving tangible growth through new branches, franchisees [E24], and responding directly to strong regional customer loyalty [E26]. The technical volatility and historical drawdown cited by the bear [E8], [E9] are clearly outpaced by a market-beating relative-strength rating of 92 [E6], a golden cross where the 50-day moving average sits above the 200-day moving average [E5], [E17], and a solid rules-based screen score of 68 out of 100 [E13]. Finally, the macroeconomic complexities and gold market challenges noted by management [E27], [E32] are balanced by operating within a Consumer Durables sector tailwind score of +0.80 [E18], [E20] featuring healthy sector median sales and profit growths of 13.0% [E22] and 17.0% [E21] respectively.

Conceded: [E25], [E26], [E28]. While the bull points to expanding market share and natural diamond demand to justify reinvestment, management's retention of capital yields a mediocre sector median ROCE of just 9.9% [E23], leaving investors with zero dividends across multiple years [E30], [E31]. Conceded: [E6], [E17]. The bull leans on a relative-strength rating of 92 [E6] and a golden cross [E17], but these technical signals ignore severe historical vulnerability marked by a devastating 66.7% peak-to-trough drawdown [E8] and an annualized volatility of 63.9% [E9]. Furthermore, citing a controlling promoter stake [E1] glosses over a steady and substantial insider dilution of 26.47 percentage points down to 73.53% [E1]. Finally, the reliance on a sector tailwind score of +0.80 [E18], [E20] fails to offset management's own admissions regarding complex economic landscapes, inflation, and unpredictable gold trajectories [E27], [E32] that drive an exceptionally weak Sharpe ratio of 0.24 [E10].
